cards.front: What kind of system call insights is
cards.back: A data pipeline more than a web service: third-party sources, heavy media, expensive GPU steps and a soft deadline per call.

cards.front: Recording volume for 10k reps × 5 calls of 50 minutes
cards.back: 50k calls, 2.5M minutes, about 42k hours of recordings a day.

cards.front: Video vs audio storage per day
cards.back: 720p video at about 0.5 GB an hour is about 21 TB a day; audio at about 30 MB an hour is about 1.3 TB. Keep video briefly, audio and transcripts longer.

cards.front: GPU pool size for the peak hour
cards.back: At about 40× real time, roughly 90-100 GPUs cover the peak hour within the 30-minute deadline (about 1,050 GPU hours a day).
step(call_id, input_uri) returns an output_uri, idempotent by (call_id, step), so a retry or duplicate just overwrites the same output.

cards.front: Why poll if vendors send webhooks?
cards.back: Webhooks get lost. A reconciler lists each tenant's recent recordings every 15 minutes and enqueues any unseen.

cards.front: Idempotency key for ingesting a recording
cards.back: The vendor's recording id, so triple-delivered webhooks plus the reconciler start one workflow.

cards.front: Why a workflow engine over cron or plain queues
cards.back: Per-call state, retries with backoff, timeouts and deadlines are built in, and each step's worker pool (CPU or GPU) scales on its own.

cards.front: Why store the model name and version with every output
cards.back: So recent calls can be reprocessed at low priority when a better model ships, without disturbing the 30-minute path.
Start with a hosted API; at 2.5M minutes a day, self-hosting an open model on your own GPUs is usually much cheaper.

cards.front: How calls are linked to deals
cards.back: Separate internal and external participants, map external emails to CRM contacts and accounts, pick the open deal, record a confidence and ask the rep when low.
Heartbeats retry crashed tasks elsewhere, vendor errors back off with jitter, and after N attempts the call goes to a dead-letter queue for replay.

quiz.q: Insights for afternoon calls arrive after 90 minutes, though the daily GPU average looks fine. What went wrong in sizing?
choices: The pool was sized for the daily average instead of the business-hours peak
The CRM matcher is too strict
quiz.why: 70% of calls end in an 8-hour window, so size for the peak hour.

quiz.q: One tenant's ingest drops to zero while others are fine. What is the most likely cause?
choices: Broken OAuth or lost webhooks for that tenant
quiz.why: Expected vs ingested per tenant catches lost webhooks and broken OAuth.

quiz.q: Zoom delivers the same recording.completed webhook three times and the reconciler also finds it. How many workflows start?
choices: One, keyed by the vendor's recording id
quiz.why: The recording id is the idempotency key.

quiz.q: A transcription worker crashes halfway through a long call. What happens?
choices: The whole pipeline restarts from download
A missed heartbeat makes the engine retry the task elsewhere; idempotent outputs make it safe
quiz.why: Long tasks heartbeat and outputs overwrite by (call_id, step).

quiz.q: A corrupt recording fails extraction every time. What should happen after N attempts?
choices: Send it to a dead-letter queue with the error and alert, so it can be replayed once fixed
quiz.why: Persistent failures go to dead letters for replay.

quiz.q: Storage bills are heading toward petabytes a year. What change has the biggest effect?
choices: Lifecycle rules deleting raw video after 30-90 days while keeping audio and transcripts
quiz.why: Video is about 21 TB a day; audio is 1.3 TB and transcripts are tiny.

quiz.q: A new sentiment model ships. How do you apply it to last month's calls?
choices: Pause new calls and reprocess everything
Only use it on new calls forever
Reprocess in the background at low priority, recording the model version
Overwrite old outputs without a version
quiz.why: Versioned outputs let reprocessing run without disturbing the deadline for new calls.
